entries.meaning: A woven or knitted cloth, especially one made in a factory. ---
examples: The town's economy ran on textiles for a hundred years.
She studies textile design at art school.
Cheap imported textiles put the old mill out of business.

entries.meaning: Weave has 2 distinct senses.
examples: This shirt has a tight weave, so the wind doesn't get through.
Hold it up to the light and you can see the weave.
Linen and cotton take very different weaves.
She got a weave before the wedding.
A good weave can last a couple of months.
The salon does braids, weaves, and color.

senses.head: The way the threads of a fabric are crossed over each other
examples: This shirt has a tight weave, so the wind doesn't get through.
Hold it up to the light and you can see the weave.
Linen and cotton take very different weaves.

senses.head: Lengths of extra hair sewn or glued into a person's own hair
examples: She got a weave before the wedding.
A good weave can last a couple of months.
The salon does braids, weaves, and color.

entries.русский: переплетение (нитей), плетение; накладные пряди, вплетённые волосы

entries.meaning: A fabric or garment made by looping yarn rather than weaving it. ---
examples: In the fall she lives in soft knits and jeans.
That sweater is a loose knit, so it stretches.
The store keeps the knits on the back wall.
entries.contrast: The k is silent — knit sounds exactly like nit.

entries.meaning: A smooth fabric that is shiny on one side and dull on the other. ---
examples: Her wedding dress was ivory satin.
The box was lined with black satin.
Satin slips off the hanger if you're not careful.
entries.contrast: Not the Russian сатин — English satin is атлас; сатин is sateen.

entries.meaning: A cotton fabric woven to give a soft sheen like satin. ---
examples: These sheets are cotton sateen.
Sateen feels cool against the skin.
She picked a sateen lining for the coat.
entries.contrast: Stress on the second syllable, sa-TEEN, unlike satin (SAT-uhn).

entries.meaning: A thick cotton fabric with raised ridges running down it. ---
examples: He wore brown corduroy pants to the interview.
Corduroy wears out at the knees first.
The jacket is lined corduroy, good for November.
entries.contrast: False friend: Russian вельвет is English corduroy, while English velvet is бархат.

entries.meaning: A rough woolen cloth woven from flecked yarn. ---
examples: My grandfather's tweed jacket still fits me.
The professor showed up in gray tweed.
Tweed is scratchy but it lasts forever.

entries.meaning: A very light, sheer fabric of silk or synthetic thread. ---
examples: The sleeves were pale pink chiffon.
Chiffon snags on everything.
She threw a chiffon scarf over her shoulders.
entries.contrast: Stress falls on the second syllable in American English: shih-FAHN.

entries.meaning: A plain cotton cloth, often used for test garments or straining food. ---
examples: Strain the broth through a piece of muslin.
She sews the first version in cheap muslin.
The curtains are unbleached muslin.

entries.meaning: A coarse brown cloth woven from jute, used for sacks and wrapping. ---
examples: The coffee came in burlap sacks.
We wrapped the tree roots in burlap.
She made table runners out of burlap.
entries.contrast: Americans say burlap; the British call the same cloth hessian.

entries.meaning: A cotton cloth woven in a small checked pattern, usually white and one color. ---
examples: The diner had red gingham on every table.
She wore a blue gingham dress.
Gingham always looks like summer to me.
entries.contrast: The gh is not an h sound: say GING-uhm, never ging-HAM.

entries.meaning: A Scottish checked pattern in which each clan has its own design. ---
examples: The band marched in full tartan.
Each family has its own tartan.
She collects scarves in old tartans.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: A strong fabric woven so that diagonal lines show on the surface. ---
examples: The pants are cotton twill.
Twill holds a crease better than plain weave.
He ordered a jacket in navy twill.

entries.meaning: A weave whose short diagonal rows change direction, like the bones of a fish. ---
examples: He had on a gray herringbone coat.
The suit is herringbone, not solid.
Herringbone reads as a texture from across the room.

entries.meaning: A checked pattern of broken, pointed shapes, usually black and white. ---
examples: She wore a houndstooth jacket.
Houndstooth never really goes out of style.
The chair was upholstered in houndstooth.

entries.meaning: A light cotton cloth with puckered stripes that keep it off the skin. ---
examples: Every summer he pulls out the seersucker suit.
Seersucker doesn't need ironing, which is the point.
The dress was blue and white seersucker.

entries.meaning: A smooth cotton fabric with fine ribs across it, common in dress shirts. ---
examples: The shirt is cotton poplin.
Poplin presses beautifully.
We ordered forty yards of white poplin.

entries.meaning: A soft knitted fabric with a short thick pile, like a stretchy velvet. ---
examples: The tracksuit was maroon velour.
Velour seats were everywhere in seventies cars.
She bought a velour robe for the winter.

entries.meaning: A fine net fabric used for veils, ballet skirts, and formal dresses. ---
examples: The skirt was layers of white tulle.
Her veil was a single piece of tulle.
Tulle catches on the slightest rough edge.
entries.contrast: One syllable, and a homophone of tool.

entries.meaning: A crisp shiny fabric that rustles when it moves. ---
examples: Her prom dress was green taffeta.
You could hear the taffeta from the hallway.
The lining is taffeta, so it slides on easily.

entries.meaning: A thin, stiff, transparent fabric used for overlays and trim. ---
examples: The sleeves were sheer organza.
She wrapped the gift in organza.
Organza holds its shape better than chiffon.

entries.meaning: A heavy fabric woven with a raised pattern, often in gold or silver thread. ---
examples: The chairs were covered in gold brocade.
She wore a jacket of stiff red brocade.
Brocade is too heavy for a summer dress.

entries.meaning: A reversible fabric whose pattern is formed by the weave itself. ---
examples: The table was set with white damask.
Damask napkins come out for the holidays.
The curtains are heavy blue damask.

entries.meaning: Calico has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The quilt is pieced from old calico.
She sewed the girls matching calico dresses.
Calico was what everyone wore on the frontier.
Our calico sleeps on the windowsill all day.
Almost all calicos are female.
The shelter had two kittens and an older calico.

senses.head: A cotton cloth printed with a small pattern, often in flowers
examples: The quilt is pieced from old calico.
She sewed the girls matching calico dresses.
Calico was what everyone wore on the frontier.

senses.head: A cat with a coat of white, black, and orange patches
examples: Our calico sleeps on the windowsill all day.
Almost all calicos are female.
The shelter had two kittens and an older calico.

entries.contrast: In the US calico is printed cotton; in Britain it means plain unbleached cotton.

entries.meaning: A tightly woven twill that sheds water, used for coats and suits. ---
examples: His raincoat was tan gabardine.
Gabardine holds a sharp crease.
The tailor recommended wool gabardine for the trousers.

entries.meaning: Crepe has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The dress is black wool crepe.
Crepe hangs well and doesn't cling.
She lined the jacket with silk crepe.
She ordered a crepe with ham and cheese.
The stand sells crepes with lemon and sugar.
He can flip a crepe without a spatula.

senses.head: A fabric with a lightly crinkled surface that drapes softly
examples: The dress is black wool crepe.
Crepe hangs well and doesn't cling.
She lined the jacket with silk crepe.

senses.head: A very thin pancake, usually rolled or folded around a filling
examples: She ordered a crepe with ham and cheese.
The stand sells crepes with lemon and sugar.
He can flip a crepe without a spatula.

entries.русский: креп (ткань с зернистой поверхностью); блинчик, креп
entries.contrast: Rhymes with tape, not with creep.

entries.meaning: A closely woven cotton cloth with a crisp, matte finish, used for sheets. ---
examples: We switched to cotton percale sheets.
Percale feels cool the first night after washing.
The hotel uses white percale on every bed.

entries.meaning: Wool yarn or cloth made from long fibers combed straight before spinning. ---
examples: The suit is fine worsted wool.
She knits mostly in worsted.
Worsted is smoother than ordinary woolen cloth.
entries.contrast: Say WUUS-tid — the first syllable sounds like wood, not like word.

entries.meaning: A silky wool from the angora goat, used in fluffy sweaters and coats. ---
examples: She wore a pale blue mohair sweater.
Mohair sheds on everything you own.
The blanket is mohair and wool.

entries.meaning: A very soft fluffy wool that comes from angora rabbits. ---
examples: The cardigan is half angora.
Angora is warm but it pills quickly.
She spins her own angora.

entries.meaning: A fine soft wool from merino sheep, worn next to the skin. ---
examples: These socks are merino, so they don't itch.
He hikes in a merino base layer.
Merino costs more but it's worth it.

entries.meaning: Sheepskin tanned with the wool still on it, used for warm coats and boots. ---
examples: Her boots are lined with shearling.
He bought a shearling jacket for the winter.
Shearling is heavy but nothing is warmer.

entries.meaning: The skin of a sheep with the wool left on, or leather made from it. ---
examples: There was a sheepskin thrown over the chair.
The gloves are lined with sheepskin.
He sells sheepskins at the county fair.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: The skin of an animal with the fur still attached. ---
examples: Trappers sold beaver pelts to the company.
A wolf pelt hung above the fireplace.
The pelts were stretched on wooden frames.

entries.meaning: A soft fabric made from processed wood pulp rather than a natural fiber. ---
examples: The blouse is rayon, so wash it cold.
Rayon wrinkles the moment you sit down.
The label says sixty percent rayon.
entries.contrast: Americans usually say rayon where Europeans say viscose — the same fiber.

entries.meaning: A fiber made from dissolved cellulose, sold in the US mostly as rayon. ---
examples: The dress is viscose and it hangs beautifully.
Viscose loses its shape when it gets wet.
European labels list viscose instead of rayon.

entries.meaning: A synthetic fiber that stretches far and springs back into shape. ---
examples: There's five percent spandex in these jeans.
The whole team wears spandex.
A little spandex keeps the knees from bagging out.
entries.contrast: Spandex is the American word; elsewhere the same fiber is called elastane or Lycra.

entries.meaning: A synthetic cloth of extremely fine threads that picks up dust and water. ---
examples: Wipe the screen with a microfiber cloth.
The couch is microfiber, so spills wipe right off.
Microfiber towels dry much faster than cotton.
entries.contrast: Spelled microfiber in the US and microfibre in Britain.

entries.meaning: A rough plant fiber spun into rope, sacks, and coarse cloth. ---
examples: The rug is woven from jute.
Jute twine is cheap and strong.
They shipped the grain in jute bags.

entries.meaning: A tough plant fiber used for rope, canvas, and heavy cloth. ---
examples: Old ships were rigged with hemp rope.
The bag is woven hemp.
Hemp softens a lot after a few washes.

entries.meaning: The blue-flowered plant whose stems are spun into linen thread. ---
examples: Flax has been grown here for centuries.
Linen is made from flax.
The field of flax turned pale blue in June.

entries.meaning: A loose, thin cotton cloth used for straining and wrapping food. ---
examples: Line the strainer with cheesecloth.
Tie the herbs up in a square of cheesecloth.
Cheesecloth is in the aisle with the foil.

entries.meaning: Cloth coated to make it waterproof, often used on kitchen tables. ---
examples: Grandma kept oilcloth on the kitchen table.
The picnic table was covered in checked oilcloth.
Oilcloth wipes clean with a sponge.

entries.meaning: Open mesh material made of knotted or woven cord or thread. ---
examples: We put netting over the strawberries.
The hat had a bit of black netting on the brim.
Netting keeps the mosquitoes off at night.

entries.meaning: A single thread or thin length of fiber twisted with others. ---
examples: Pull out a strand of the yarn and look at it.
The rope is made of three twisted strands.
A loose strand was hanging off the sleeve.

entries.meaning: One of the strands twisted together to make a yarn or thread. ---
examples: This is a four-ply wool.
The pattern calls for a heavier ply.
Separate the plies and use just one.

entries.meaning: A loose coil of yarn as it is sold in a store. ---
examples: I need three more skeins to finish the sweater.
She wound the skein into a ball.
The skein came undone in my bag.
entries.contrast: Rhymes with cane, not with seen.

entries.meaning: A small cylinder that thread or wire is wound onto. ---
examples: Pick up a spool of black thread while you're out.
The spool rolled under the couch.
She keeps her spools sorted by color.
entries.contrast: Americans buy a spool of thread; the British buy a reel.

entries.meaning: The small spool that holds the lower thread inside a sewing machine. ---
examples: The bobbin ran out halfway down the seam.
Wind a bobbin before you start.
She keeps spare bobbins in a tin.

entries.meaning: A cylinder that thread, wire, or film is wound around. ---
examples: The mill ships the yarn on wooden reels.
He unwound a length off the reel.
Two empty reels were sitting by the loom.
entries.contrast: Homophone of real. For sewing thread, Americans normally say spool instead.

entries.meaning: Strong string made of two or more strands twisted together. ---
examples: Tie the box up with twine.
There's a ball of twine in the drawer.
The bundles were bound with twine.

entries.meaning: A small metal cap worn on the finger to push a needle through cloth. ---
examples: Use a thimble or you'll stab yourself.
Her mother's silver thimble is in the sewing box.
He collects antique thimbles.

entries.meaning: A small stuffed pad that pins and needles are stuck into. ---
examples: The pincushion is shaped like a tomato.
Stick the needle back in the pincushion.
She sews little pincushions out of scraps.

entries.meaning: A pointed hand tool for punching holes in leather or heavy cloth. ---
examples: Punch the holes with an awl first.
The old awl had a worn wooden handle.
A saddler keeps several awls on the bench.
entries.contrast: Sounds almost exactly like all; only the context tells them apart.

entries.meaning: A machine that trims a seam and stitches over its raw edge at once. ---
examples: Finish the edges on the serger.
She saved up for a serger.
Most home sewers own a machine and a serger.
entries.contrast: American serger; the British call the same machine an overlocker.

entries.meaning: A rod that twists fiber into thread and holds the thread as it is spun. ---
examples: She twisted the wool onto the spindle.
A drop spindle is the simplest way to start spinning.
The mill had rows of humming spindles.

entries.meaning: Warp has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The warp runs the length of the fabric.
It takes a whole day to set up the warp.
A broken warp thread stops the machine.
There's a slight warp in the tabletop.
Damp air put a warp in the door, and now it sticks.
Sight down the board and check it for warp.

senses.head: The lengthwise threads held on a loom while cloth is woven
examples: The warp runs the length of the fabric.
It takes a whole day to set up the warp.
A broken warp thread stops the machine.

senses.head: A bend or twist in something that should be flat or straight
examples: There's a slight warp in the tabletop.
Damp air put a warp in the door, and now it sticks.
Sight down the board and check it for warp.

entries.meaning: The crosswise threads woven over and under the warp. ---
examples: The weft is a darker blue than the warp.
She packs the weft down tight after each pass.
A loose weft makes a soft, open cloth.

entries.meaning: The finished edge of woven cloth that does not fray. ---
examples: Line the pattern up with the selvage.
The selvage has the maker's name printed on it.
Cut the selvages off before you sew.
entries.contrast: Usually spelled selvage in the US and selvedge in Britain.

entries.meaning: The bottom edge of a skirt, dress, or coat, seen as a level. ---
examples: The hemline hit just below the knee.
Hemlines went up again that spring.
She let the hemline down two inches.

entries.meaning: Dart has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Sew the darts before you join the side seams.
The dart pulls the waist in.
Two darts in the back will fix that gap.
He threw a dart and hit the bullseye.
The vet dropped the bear with a tranquilizer dart.
Three darts were still stuck in the wall.

senses.head: A tapered fold sewn into cloth so a garment fits the body's curves
examples: Sew the darts before you join the side seams.
The dart pulls the waist in.
Two darts in the back will fix that gap.

senses.head: A small pointed missile thrown at a target board or shot from a gun
examples: He threw a dart and hit the bullseye.
The vet dropped the bear with a tranquilizer dart.
Three darts were still stuck in the wall.

entries.meaning: A small piece of cloth sewn in to add room or strength. ---
examples: A gusset under the arm lets the sleeve move.
The bag has a wide gusset at the bottom.
Add gussets if the shirt feels tight across the back.

entries.meaning: Yoke has 3 distinct senses.
examples: The shirt has a western yoke across the back.
Gather the skirt into the yoke.
Both yokes are cut on the bias.
The oxen pulled the plow under a heavy wooden yoke.
He lifted the yoke off the tired pair.
The yoke had rubbed sores into their necks.
The country threw off the yoke of colonial rule.
They lived for years under the yoke of a dictator.
Poets wrote about breaking the yoke of tyranny.

senses.head: A shaped piece across the shoulders or hips that the rest of a garment hangs from
examples: The shirt has a western yoke across the back.
Gather the skirt into the yoke.
Both yokes are cut on the bias.

senses.head: A wooden frame joining two work animals at the neck so they pull together
examples: The oxen pulled the plow under a heavy wooden yoke.
He lifted the yoke off the tired pair.
The yoke had rubbed sores into their necks.

senses.head: Harsh control by another country or ruler
examples: The country threw off the yoke of colonial rule.
They lived for years under the yoke of a dictator.
Poets wrote about breaking the yoke of tyranny.

entries.русский: кокетка (деталь одежды); ярмо, хомут (для волов); иго, гнёт
entries.contrast: A homophone of yolk, the yellow of an egg.

entries.meaning: A piece of cloth sewn to an edge and turned inside to finish it neatly. ---
examples: Press the facing to the inside.
The neckline has a narrow facing.
Cut the facings from the same fabric.

entries.meaning: Stiffening material placed between two layers of cloth to give shape. ---
examples: Iron the interfacing onto the collar.
Use light interfacing so the cuff still bends.
Interfacing is what keeps a waistband from folding over.

entries.meaning: Batting has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Lay the batting between the two layers.
Cotton batting shrinks a little the first wash.
She bought a whole roll of batting.
His batting has improved a lot since spring training.
The team's batting fell apart in the second half of the season.
She leads the league in batting this year.

senses.head: A soft layer of cotton or synthetic fiber used to fill a quilt or jacket
examples: Lay the batting between the two layers.
Cotton batting shrinks a little the first wash.
She bought a whole roll of batting.

senses.head: The act or skill of hitting the ball in baseball
examples: His batting has improved a lot since spring training.
The team's batting fell apart in the second half of the season.
She leads the league in batting this year.

entries.русский: ватин, синтепон (для стёжки); отбивание мяча (в бейсболе)
entries.contrast: Same word as batting in baseball, but the quilting sense is uncountable.

entries.meaning: Padding has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The jacket has padding in the shoulders.
Pull the padding out and the coat is much lighter.
There's thin padding along the strap.
The last two pages are pure padding.
Cut the padding and the report gets much stronger.
Half his answer was padding.

senses.head: Soft material put inside cloth to give bulk, warmth, or protection
examples: The jacket has padding in the shoulders.
Pull the padding out and the coat is much lighter.
There's thin padding along the strap.

senses.head: Extra words or material added only to make something longer
examples: The last two pages are pure padding.
Cut the padding and the report gets much stronger.
Half his answer was padding.

entries.русский: набивка, мягкая прокладка; «вода», лишний текст для объёма

entries.meaning: Piping has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The cushions have white piping.
Red piping runs down the side of the trousers.
Piping makes a plain seam look finished.
The old copper piping has to be replaced.
Piping runs behind the wall to the water heater.
Rusted piping was leaking under the floor.

senses.head: A narrow cord covered in fabric and sewn into a seam as trim
examples: The cushions have white piping.
Red piping runs down the side of the trousers.
Piping makes a plain seam look finished.

senses.head: The pipes in a building or machine, taken together
examples: The old copper piping has to be replaced.
Piping runs behind the wall to the water heater.
Rusted piping was leaking under the floor.

entries.meaning: Trim has 3 distinct senses.
examples: The dress has lace trim at the collar.
Buttons and trim are down the next aisle.
A little velvet trim would dress it up.
I just want a trim, not a new style.
The hedge needs a trim before the party.
A quick trim costs twenty dollars here.
We painted the walls gray and the trim white.
The trim around the window is rotting.
New trim would make the room look finished.

senses.head: Ribbon, lace, or braid added to a garment for decoration
examples: The dress has lace trim at the collar.
Buttons and trim are down the next aisle.
A little velvet trim would dress it up.

senses.head: A light cutting that makes hair or a hedge neat without changing it much
examples: I just want a trim, not a new style.
The hedge needs a trim before the party.
A quick trim costs twenty dollars here.

senses.head: The narrow strips of wood around the doors, windows, and floor of a room
examples: We painted the walls gray and the trim white.
The trim around the window is rotting.
New trim would make the room look finished.

entries.русский: отделка, фурнитура (для одежды); подравнивание (стрижка); наличники, плинтус (отделка)

entries.meaning: A strip of gathered cloth sewn on as a decorative edge. ---
examples: The blouse has a ruffle down the front.
She hates ruffles on anything.
Add a narrow ruffle at the hem.

entries.meaning: A narrow fold of cloth stitched down to shorten or decorate a garment. ---
examples: There are three little tucks on each side.
A tuck at the waist will take it in.
Press each tuck flat before you sew the next.

entries.meaning: Stretchy cord or tape sewn into clothing so it pulls back into shape. ---
examples: The waistband has elastic in it.
Buy half an inch of elastic for the cuffs.
The elastic in these socks is shot.

entries.meaning: Eyelet has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Thread the cord through the eyelets.
One eyelet on the boot tore out.
The blouse is white cotton eyelet.
The blouse is made of white eyelet with a scalloped hem.
The curtains are trimmed with eyelet.
Eyelet is cool to wear in August.

senses.head: A small reinforced hole in cloth for a lace or cord to pass through
examples: Thread the cord through the eyelets.
One eyelet on the boot tore out.
The blouse is white cotton eyelet.

senses.head: A light cotton fabric with small holes stitched into a pattern
examples: The blouse is made of white eyelet with a scalloped hem.
The curtains are trimmed with eyelet.
Eyelet is cool to wear in August.

entries.русский: люверс; ажурная вышивка; ткань с ажурной вышивкой (бродери англез)

entries.meaning: The opening in a garment that a sleeve is set into. ---
examples: The armholes are cut too high.
Measure around the armhole before you cut the sleeve.
Finish the armhole with bias tape.

entries.meaning: The seam running from the crotch to the bottom of a trouser leg, or its length. ---
examples: What's your inseam, thirty-two?
The tailor took an inch off the inseam.
Both inseams had come unstitched.
entries.русский: внутренний шов брючины (длина по внутренней стороне)
entries.contrast: Americans ask for an inseam; the British ask for the inside leg.

entries.meaning: The line around a garment or body at the narrowest part of the middle. ---
examples: The dress has a high waistline.
Waistlines dropped in the twenties.
Mark the waistline with chalk.
entries.contrast: Waist sounds exactly like waste.

entries.meaning: A tiny shiny disc sewn onto cloth for decoration. ---
examples: The top was covered in silver sequins.
A sequin came off and rolled under the table.
Sequins get everywhere once they start falling off.

entries.meaning: A person's initials combined into one design and stitched onto cloth. ---
examples: His shirts have a small monogram on the pocket.
The towels came with our monogram.
She embroiders monograms on baby blankets.

entries.meaning: Sewing and embroidery done by hand, especially as a craft. ---
examples: Her needlework hangs in the front hall.
Needlework was taught in every girls' school then.
He has no patience for needlework.
entries.contrast: Uncountable — say a piece of needlework, never a needlework.

entries.meaning: The craft of stitching layers of cloth and filling together. ---
examples: She took up quilting after she retired.
The quilting on this blanket is all done by hand.
There's a quilting class at the library.

entries.meaning: Sewing that joins small pieces of different fabrics into one cloth. ---
examples: The quilt is patchwork in reds and blues.
She makes bags out of patchwork.
Patchwork uses up every last scrap.

entries.meaning: The craft of making cloth by looping yarn with two long needles. ---
examples: She brought her knitting on the train.
Knitting keeps my hands busy.
He put the knitting down and answered the door.
entries.contrast: The k is silent: NIT-ing.

entries.meaning: The craft of making cloth by pulling loops of yarn through with a hook. ---
examples: The blanket is crochet, not knitting.
She learned crochet from her aunt.
There's a crochet border around the edge.
entries.contrast: The final t is silent and ch is a sh sound: kroh-SHAY.

entries.meaning: The making of cloth by crossing threads over and under each other. ---
examples: She teaches weaving at the craft school.
Weaving is slow work on a hand loom.
The museum has a room about weaving.

entries.meaning: The work of joining or mending cloth with a needle and thread. ---
examples: There's a pile of sewing on the table.
I do all my sewing on Sunday afternoons.
She keeps her sewing things in a wicker basket.
entries.contrast: Sew rhymes with so, not with sue — so it is SOH-ing, not SOO-ing.

entries.meaning: A row or set of stitches, seen as the sewing on a finished item. ---
examples: The stitching on the pocket came loose.
You can see the stitching from the outside.
Contrast stitching is what makes jeans look like jeans.

entries.meaning: Basting has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Pull the basting out once the seam is done.
A little basting saves a lot of ripping later.
The basting is in white thread so it shows.
Frequent basting keeps the turkey from drying out.
The basting liquid was butter, wine, and herbs.
Give it one more basting before it comes out.

senses.head: Long loose stitches that hold cloth in place until it is sewn properly
examples: Pull the basting out once the seam is done.
A little basting saves a lot of ripping later.
The basting is in white thread so it shows.

senses.head: The spooning of juices or fat over meat while it roasts
examples: Frequent basting keeps the turkey from drying out.
The basting liquid was butter, wine, and herbs.
Give it one more basting before it comes out.

entries.русский: намётка (временные стежки); поливание жиром/соком при запекании

entries.meaning: A knitting stitch made by pulling the yarn toward you, the opposite of a knit stitch. ---
examples: Knit one, purl two, all the way across.
The ribbing is knits and purls.
